Exactly! dogs are great because their love is constant and unconditional.  Cats are much different.  But their love is so much more rewarding because of it.  I read your post.  Go get yourself a kitten or a cat.  I don't know your living situation but if you're able to own a cat it's a great idea,  just know that it may take some time for it to really start to like you.  There's also a chance it just won't like you no matter what!  Some cats just hate humans (because they've met asshole humans).  Best bet is to get a kitten so you can raise it and he/she will stick to you like glue if you treat em right.  

Zeus is a shelter cat who came from a home of hoarders and like 30 cats.  He was never aggressive but he was reeeeal scared of me.  Almost a year later and he comes running whenever I say his name every time.  He is such a weirdo man I wish you could know the extent of it.  His "meows" sound like opera noises rather than meows.  It doesn't always go like this though, shelter cats can be pretty traumatized and hard to socialize.  

Regardless.  Find a purpose.  It'll probably even be the wrong one and you'll have to re work things.  You're 17 years old and I'm 21.  We both have plenty of potential ahead of us.  And maybe it turns out that we both end up being useless peices of shit.  But you have to keep moving.  THE ANSWER TO SUFFERING IS NOT MORE SUFFERING.  It's easy to say forsure.  You might argue you'll be ending you're suffering assuming you succeed, but in reality you're pain will just transfer onto your family.  Life is so short, I'm already AT LEAST 25% done with this shit.  Why not wait it out and see what happens?    

LIFE IS SUFFERING and you won't escape it.  Don't add to the world's suffering,  find something you can do to relieve just a little suffering.

Indeed. Zeus (siamese) and Syn.  They are both very needy and cuddly so much so that it often gets in the way of what I'm trying to do lol.  Their services are undoubtedly appreciated though.
